# Context7 MCP Server for VS Code

Source: https://github.com/upstash/context7-vscode-extension/blob/master/README.md

# Context7 MCP Server for VS Code

This VS Code extension registers the [Context7](https://context7.com) MCP (Model Context Protocol) server with VS Code's built-in MCP support, giving AI assistants real-time access to up-to-date documentation for thousands of libraries and frameworks.

The extension connects to the hosted Context7 server at `https://mcp.context7.com/mcp`, so it is always running the latest version — no local server process, no manual updates.

## Features

- **Up-to-date Documentation**: Pulls version-specific documentation and code examples straight from the source into your AI assistant's context
- **Automatic Library Resolution**: Finds the right library documentation based on your query
- **Zero Configuration**: The server is registered automatically when the extension activates
- **Optional API Key**: Add a Context7 API key for higher rate limits and access to private repositories

## Installation

Install **Context7 MCP Server** from the [Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=Upstash.context7-mcp), or from the Extensions view in VS Code (`Upstash.context7-mcp`).

Requires VS Code 1.101 or later.

## Usage

Once installed, the Context7 MCP server is available to VS Code's AI features (e.g. Copilot Chat in agent mode). Ask questions like:

- "Show me how to use React hooks. use context7"
- "What are the best practices for Next.js routing? use context7"
- "How do I implement authentication with Supabase? use context7"

You can also reference a library directly by its Context7 ID:

```text
Implement basic authentication with Supabase. Use the API and documentation from the /supabase/supabase library.
```

> **Tip:** Add a rule to your AI assistant's instructions (e.g. `.github/copilot-instructions.md`) telling it to use Context7 for code generation and library questions, so you don't have to type `use context7` every time.

### Available Tools

1. **`resolve-library-id`** — Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID
2. **`get-library-docs`** — Fetches up-to-date documentation for a library

## Configuration

| Setting | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `context7.apiKey` | Optional Context7 API key for higher rate limits and private repositories. Get one at [context7.com/dashboard](https://context7.com/dashboard). |

Changing the API key stops the running server so the new key can be picked up. Restart it via **MCP: List Servers** → **Context7** → **Start Server** (or just send a new chat request, which prompts to start it) — no window reload required.

## Development

### Project Structure

```text
├── src/
│   └── extension.ts          # Main extension code
├── package.json              # Extension manifest
├── tsconfig.json             # TypeScript configuration
├── CHANGELOG.md              # Release notes
├── DEPLOYMENT.md             # Publishing guide
└── README.md                 # This file
```

### Building

```bash
npm install     # Install dependencies
npm run compile # Build the extension
```

### Testing

1. Open this repository in VS Code
2. Press F5 to launch the extension in a new Extension Development Host window
3. Run the **MCP: List Servers** command and confirm "Context7" is listed
4. Open Copilot Chat in agent mode and ask a library question with "use context7"

# Deployment Guide for Context7 VS Code Extension

Source: https://github.com/upstash/context7-vscode-extension/blob/master/DEPLOYMENT.md

# Deployment Guide for Context7 VS Code Extension

This guide explains how to build, test, and publish the Context7 VS Code extension to the Visual Studio Code Marketplace.

The extension is published as [`Upstash.context7-mcp`](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=Upstash.context7-mcp) under the verified **Upstash** publisher.

## Build and Test Locally

```bash
npm install      # Install dependencies
npm run compile  # Type-check and build to out/
```

To test interactively: open this repository in VS Code, press F5 to launch an Extension Development Host, then run the **MCP: List Servers** command and confirm "Context7" appears. Ask Copilot Chat (agent mode) a library question with "use context7" to verify end to end.

To test the packaged artifact:

```bash
npx @vscode/vsce package                              # Produces context7-mcp-<version>.vsix
code --install-extension context7-mcp-<version>.vsix  # Install into your regular VS Code
```

## Publishing

### Automated (recommended)

Pushing a `v*` tag triggers `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, which builds and publishes to the Marketplace:

```bash
# 1. Bump "version" in package.json and add a CHANGELOG.md entry, commit, push
# 2. Tag and push the tag
git tag v1.1.0
git push origin v1.1.0
```

The workflow requires a repository secret named `VSCE_PAT` containing an Azure DevOps Personal Access Token with the **Marketplace (Publish)** scope, created by a member of the Upstash publisher. See [Publishing Extensions](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/working-with-extensions/publishing-extension#get-a-personal-access-token) for how to create one. Marketplace PATs expire (max 1 year) — rotate the secret when publishing starts failing with authentication errors.

### Manual

```bash
npm install
npx @vscode/vsce publish
```

You will be prompted for the publisher Personal Access Token. `vsce` runs `vscode:prepublish` (the compile step) automatically.

To bump the version as part of publishing:

```bash
npx @vscode/vsce publish patch  # 1.1.0 → 1.1.1
npx @vscode/vsce publish minor  # 1.1.0 → 1.2.0
npx @vscode/vsce publish major  # 1.1.0 → 2.0.0
```

## Version Management

Follow semantic versioning:

- **Patch** (1.1.1): Bug fixes
- **Minor** (1.2.0): New features, backward compatible
- **Major** (2.0.0): Breaking changes

Record every release in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Post-Publishing

- Check the extension's Marketplace page for reviews and ratings
- Monitor download statistics
- Respond to user feedback and GitHub issues

## Troubleshooting

1. **Authentication errors**: Ensure the Personal Access Token is valid, unexpired, and has the Marketplace (Publish) scope
2. **Packaging errors**: Run `npm run compile` first and check for TypeScript errors
3. **Server not appearing in VS Code**: Confirm VS Code ≥ 1.101 and check the **MCP: List Servers** command

## Resources

- [VS Code Extension Publishing Guide](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/working-with-extensions/publishing-extension)
- [VS Code MCP Developer Guide](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/extension-guides/ai/mcp)
- [vsce Documentation](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-vsce)
